content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: overtime, callback, cross-skilled moves and a break shift. It is the best available plan, lifting service level to 74.3% for 12:30-16:00, but still short of the 80% target.","why":"Payments calls jumped after the 10:55 reward-points email to 500,000 card holders. They reached +52% at 11:30 (164 vs 108 expected) and service level fell to 32%. With no action, the 12:30-16:00 window is predicted at 64.9% (Payments 56.4%) with 8.5% abandons. P3 offers overtime to 9 Payments agents 13:00-15:00 and runs IVR callback on Payments 12:30-15:30. It also moves 2 then 3 cross-skilled agents from General 14:00-16:00 and delays Payments breaks 14:15-15:15 by 45 minutes. That lifts the window to 74.3% (Payments 68.9%, General 86.7%) and cuts abandons to 5.6%, for ₹2,160. No plan reaches 80% in the window, and P3 scores highest. Rest of day is predicted at 82.2%. The campaign link is medium confidence: the timing and audience fit, but the email is about card rewards rather than payments.","trade_offs":["P2 costs the same ₹2,160 but reaches only 70.9% (Payments 64.0%) with 6.2% abandons. P3 adds the free moves and break shift on top of it.","P1 costs nothing but reaches only 67.1% (Payments 60.2%) and pulls General down to 83.0%.","R1 also costs ₹2,160 and moves more General agents, but scores slightly lower overall at 73.9%, with General at 85.1%.","R2 costs ₹2,835 and cancels General coaching for 74.2%, which is no better than P3.","General stays healthy under P3 at 86.7%, so the agent moves carry little risk to that queue."],"watch":"Check Payments volume against forecast every 15 minutes. If calls keep climbing past +52%, or General drops toward 80% once the moves start at 14:00, re-plan. Confirm overtime uptake from the 9 agents before 13:00."}
